This report outlines how Saskatoon Transit has worked to strengthen information and communication on notices for digital, phone and paper approaches for changes to bus routes, including recent engagement activities undertaken with stakeholders.
Paper service alert notices are used when the stop will be closed for at least 24 hours or when there is a large impact to riders due to a traffic detour.
A supervisor post the paper notice at affected stops the day before takes effect.
These notices contain information regarding start date of the interruption, the location of the next serviceable bus stop and information to find digital tools.

Administration recently engaged stakeholder groups through our facility through four facilitated in-person sessions and an online survey to gather feedback on Saskatoon Transit's current service alerts and suggestions for improvements.

Participants in the four facilitated in-person sessions including organizations representing people who take transit that are experiencing disabilities, indigenous peoples, newcomers, seniors and youth and people with living experiences of systemic barriers.
What we heard was that they are more likely to depend on paper notices or phone and goal for information about changes to their bus route than digital service alerts.
There were few complaints about the current paper notices.
The main method for administering the online survey was through the Transit app and approximately 90% of respondents said they use the Transit app every day or a couple of times a week.
In general, users who subscribe to service alerts and the Transit app find them relatively easy to understand and helpful.
An engagement summary is provided in appendix one.
Saskatoon Transit is a recently addressed or as plans in place to continue to strengthen information and communication on service alert notices based on outcomes from the engagement sessions.
Several initiatives are outlined in the report and additional responses to what we heard from the engagement summary are in appendix two.

As for next steps, feedback from this engagement summary will be shared with participants and the Saskatoon Transit staff to further the conversation about strengthening service alerts and communications with riders.
Saskatoon Transit will continue refining digital notifications to provide clear and concise information to transit riders.
In addition, paper notifications will continue to be posted at bus stops for detours and closures longer than 24 hours.
